title: Pharmacy business licensing and ownership regime (Queensland)
summary: The Pharmacy Business Ownership Act 2024 created the Queensland Pharmacy Business Ownership Council (from 1 September 2024) and, from 1 November 2025, commenced the remaining provisions on pharmacy business ownership, material interests, licensing and enforcement.

commenced.what: Council established (most of Parts 1-2, 9-13) (2024 SL No. 193)
Remaining provisions incl. ownership, licensing and enforcement (2025 SL No. 130)

direction_rationale: A new licensing layer and enforced ownership restrictions add compliance costs and limit who may own pharmacies, raising barriers to entry and expansion.

industries.name: Pharmaceutical, Cosmetic and Toiletry Goods Retailing

comparison: Other states' pharmacy ownership regimes (unchanged in 2025)
confounders: Commonwealth 8th Community Pharmacy Agreement from 1 Jul 2025
notes: Too recent for annual CABEE before ~2027.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. assessment.summary: A new licensing regime and council enforce Queensland's rules on who may own a pharmacy. It adds a licensing layer and tightens enforcement of ownership limits that keep out other business models.

marks.reason: A new pharmacy business licence and enforced ownership limits restrict who may open or buy a pharmacy.
Owners must hold a licence and report material interests.
